# Overview

**Overview, `mg/L`.** `n` = 48,787 measurements in 4 groups below this sub-compartment.

@fig-aquatic-freshwater-mg-l shows a significant range of variation in measured copper concentrations in Arctic and Norwegian freshwaters. At first glance, both lotic (n = 41,831 + 1102, 2 sources) and lentic (n = 6,847, 1 source) waters are most frequently in the 1e-4 - 1e-2 mg/L range, between the M608 background (I) and good (II) quality classes. Lotic waters show substantially more variation, with measured concentrations varying between 1e-7 to perhaps as high as 1e+3 mg/L, while lentic waters vary between 1e-06 and 1e01 mg/L. Artificial water has a far smaller sample size (n = 3, 1 source)

# Groups

## G001-Wfw-Rwc-C Aquatic / Freshwater / River, stream, canal / Water column, pelagic zone / mg/L {#grp-G001-Wfw-Rwc-C}

`G001-Wfw-Rwc-C` `n` = 41,831 measurements, from **1** source (distinct `REFERENCE_ID`). Unit: `mg/L`.

@fig-g001-wfw-rwc-c shows a clear multimopdal (a) distribution of copper concentrations between background (I) and good (III) threshholds. A possible weak time trend is apparent (b) but not confirmable without additional evidence. Plotting distributions by campaign (c) shows a clear effect on concentration distributions: Measured Monitoring, Pollution Monitoring, and Road Traffic Impact show roughly log-normal distributions between M-608 classes I and II, but Mine Impact displays a distinctly flatter log-normal distribution that drags the right tail of the overall distribution as high as 1e3 mg/L; that is, copper in the g/L range. Although mine sites may be expected to be extremely contaminated, this seems improbably high, and possibly represents a unit error.

The vast majority of samples are coded as taken from *Water column, pelagic zone* (d). Because in *Water surface* and *Other* fall well within the distribution of the former, it seems valid to lump these together under the former. (e) shows no detectable spatial variation in concentrations at the resolution assessed.

::: callout-warning
## Flagged

- **multimodal** (dip test not run)
:::

## G003-Wfw-Lwc-C Aquatic / Freshwater / Lake, pond, pool, reservoir / Water column, pelagic zone / mg/L {#grp-G003-Wfw-Lwc-C}

`G003-Wfw-Lwc-C` `n` = 6,847 measurements, from **1** source (distinct `REFERENCE_ID`). Unit: `mg/L`.

::: callout-warning
## Flagged

- **multimodal** (dip test not run)
:::

@fig-g003-wfw-lwc-c-a shows a clearly multi-modal distribution clustered around a mean of mu ± sd (n = n, m sources). Small peaks are seen at approximately 1e-4 and 1e+00, the former likely a true distribution but the latter probably a unit error. @fig-g003-wfw-lwc-c-b suggests that the leftmost peak seen is from sampling in the 2018-2019 period that returned a mean copper concentration below background levels, more recent samples (2019 onwards) are centred around a the 1e-03 point. @fig-g003-wfw-lwc-c-c shows a similar pattern of distributions across campaigns, where the Mine Impact monitoring campaign reports concentrations orders of magnitude higher than other campaigns with larger sample sizes. @fig-g003-wfw-lwc-c-d shows no apparent difference between sub-geographies, while @fig-g003-wfw-lwc-c-e shows no spatial variation at the analysed resolution.
